def _apply_parsed_cooklang_to_recipe_data(data, parsed, fallback_title=""):
    title = parsed.title or fallback_title
    if title:
        data["title"] = title
    data["description"] = parsed.description
    data["prep_time_minutes"] = parsed.prep_time_minutes
    data["cook_time_minutes"] = parsed.cook_time_minutes
    data["servings"] = parsed.servings
    data["difficulty"] = parsed.difficulty
    data["source_url"] = parsed.source_url
    data["cooklang_parse_status"] = "VALID"
    data["cooklang_parse_error"] = ""


def _create_cooklang_children(recipe, parsed):
    for ingredient in parsed.ingredients:
        RecipeIngredient.objects.create(
            recipe=recipe,
            name=ingredient.name,
            amount=ingredient.amount,
            unit=ingredient.unit,
            notes=ingredient.notes,
            order=ingredient.order,
        )
    for step in parsed.steps:
        RecipeStep.objects.create(
            recipe=recipe,
            instruction=step.instruction,
            timer_minutes=step.timer_minutes,
            order=step.order,
        )


class RecipeCreateSerializer(serializers.ModelSerializer):
    """Serializer for creating recipes."""

    ingredients = RecipeIngredientCreateSerializer(many=True, required=False)
    steps = RecipeStepCreateSerializer(many=True, required=False)
    draft_id = serializers.UUIDField(required=False, write_only=True)

    class Meta:
        model = Recipe
        fields = [
            "id",
            "title",
            "description",
            "family",
            "prep_time_minutes",
            "cook_time_minutes",
            "servings",
            "difficulty",
            "source_url",
            "cooklang_source",
            "cooklang_parse_status",
            "cooklang_parse_error",
            "ingredients",
            "steps",
            "draft_id",
        ]
        read_only_fields = ["id", "cooklang_parse_status", "cooklang_parse_error"]
        extra_kwargs = {"title": {"required": False, "allow_blank": True}}

    def validate_family(self, value):
        """Ensure user is a member of the family."""
        request = self.context.get("request")
        assert request is not None
        user = request.user

        if not FamilyMembership.objects.filter(
            user=user, family=value, is_active=True
        ).exists():
            raise serializers.ValidationError(
                "You can only create recipes for families you belong to."
            )
        return value

    def validate(self, attrs):
        """Parse Cooklang source when provided and project it into recipe fields."""
        source = attrs.get("cooklang_source")
        if source is not None and source.strip():
            try:
                parsed = parse_cooklang_source(source)
            except ValueError as exc:
                raise serializers.ValidationError(
                    {"cooklang_source": str(exc)}
                ) from exc

            _apply_parsed_cooklang_to_recipe_data(
                attrs, parsed, fallback_title=attrs.get("title", "")
            )
            attrs["_parsed_cooklang"] = parsed

        if not attrs.get("title"):
            raise serializers.ValidationError(
                {
                    "title": (
                        "This field is required unless cooklang_source has "
                        "title metadata."
                    )
                }
            )

        return attrs

    def create(self, validated_data):
        """Create recipe with nested ingredients and steps."""
        from django.db import transaction

        from .services import RecipePhotoService

        ingredients_data = validated_data.pop("ingredients", [])
        steps_data = validated_data.pop("steps", [])
        parsed_cooklang = validated_data.pop("_parsed_cooklang", None)
        draft_id = validated_data.pop("draft_id", None)
        request = self.context.get("request")
        assert request is not None

        with transaction.atomic():
            # Create the recipe
            recipe = Recipe.objects.create(author=request.user, **validated_data)

            if parsed_cooklang is not None:
                _create_cooklang_children(recipe, parsed_cooklang)
            else:
                # Create ingredients
                for idx, ingredient_data in enumerate(ingredients_data):
                    if "order" not in ingredient_data:
                        ingredient_data["order"] = idx
                    RecipeIngredient.objects.create(recipe=recipe, **ingredient_data)

                # Create steps
                for idx, step_data in enumerate(steps_data):
                    if "order" not in step_data:
                        step_data["order"] = idx
                    RecipeStep.objects.create(recipe=recipe, **step_data)

            # Copy screenshot from draft if provided
            if draft_id:
                try:
                    user = request.user
                    draft = RecipeDraft.objects.get(id=draft_id, creator=user)
                    if draft.screenshot:
                        RecipePhotoService.copy_draft_screenshot_to_recipe(
                            draft, recipe, user
                        )
                except RecipeDraft.DoesNotExist:
                    logger.warning(f"Draft {draft_id} not found for recipe creation")
                except Exception as e:
                    logger.error(f"Failed to copy draft screenshot: {e}")

        return recipe


class RecipeUpdateSerializer(serializers.ModelSerializer):
    """Serializer for updating recipes."""

    ingredients = RecipeIngredientCreateSerializer(many=True, required=False)
    steps = RecipeStepCreateSerializer(many=True, required=False)

    class Meta:
        model = Recipe
        fields = [
            "title",
            "description",
            "prep_time_minutes",
            "cook_time_minutes",
            "servings",
            "difficulty",
            "source_url",
            "cooklang_source",
            "cooklang_parse_status",
            "cooklang_parse_error",
            "ingredients",
            "steps",
        ]
        read_only_fields = ["cooklang_parse_status", "cooklang_parse_error"]
        extra_kwargs = {"title": {"allow_blank": True}}

    def validate(self, attrs):
        """Parse Cooklang edits and project them onto the existing recipe."""
        source = attrs.get("cooklang_source")
        if source is None:
            if attrs.get("title") == "":
                raise serializers.ValidationError(
                    {"title": "This field may not be blank."}
                )
            return attrs

        if not source.strip():
            attrs["cooklang_parse_status"] = "NONE"
            attrs["cooklang_parse_error"] = ""
            return attrs

        try:
            parsed = parse_cooklang_source(source)
        except ValueError as exc:
            raise serializers.ValidationError({"cooklang_source": str(exc)}) from exc

        fallback_title = attrs.get("title", "") or getattr(self.instance, "title", "")
        _apply_parsed_cooklang_to_recipe_data(
            attrs, parsed, fallback_title=fallback_title
        )
        attrs["_parsed_cooklang"] = parsed

        return attrs

    def update(self, instance, validated_data):
        """Update recipe with nested ingredients and steps."""
        from django.db import transaction

        ingredients_data = validated_data.pop("ingredients", None)
        steps_data = validated_data.pop("steps", None)
        parsed_cooklang = validated_data.pop("_parsed_cooklang", None)

        with transaction.atomic():
            # Update recipe fields
            for attr, value in validated_data.items():
                setattr(instance, attr, value)
            instance.save()

            if parsed_cooklang is not None:
                instance.ingredients.all().delete()
                instance.steps.all().delete()
                _create_cooklang_children(instance, parsed_cooklang)
                return instance

            # Replace ingredients if provided
            if ingredients_data is not None:
                instance.ingredients.all().delete()
                for idx, ingredient_data in enumerate(ingredients_data):
                    if "order" not in ingredient_data:
                        ingredient_data["order"] = idx
                    RecipeIngredient.objects.create(recipe=instance, **ingredient_data)

            # Replace steps if provided
            if steps_data is not None:
                instance.steps.all().delete()
                for idx, step_data in enumerate(steps_data):
                    if "order" not in step_data:
                        step_data["order"] = idx
                    RecipeStep.objects.create(recipe=instance, **step_data)

        return instance


class RecipeShareSerializer(serializers.Serializer):
    """Serializer for sharing recipes to other families."""

    family_ids = serializers.ListField(
        child=serializers.UUIDField(),
        required=False,
        help_text="List of family IDs to share with",
    )
    meta_family_ids = serializers.ListField(
        child=serializers.UUIDField(),
        required=False,
        help_text="List of meta family IDs to share with",
    )

    def validate_family_ids(self, value):
        """Validate that user can share to these families."""
        if not value:
            return value
        request = self.context.get("request")
        assert request is not None
        user = request.user

        # Get user's families
        user_family_ids = set(
            FamilyMembership.objects.filter(user=user, is_active=True).values_list(
                "family_id", flat=True
            )
        )

        # Validate all requested families exist and user is a member
        requested_ids = set(value)
        invalid_ids = requested_ids - user_family_ids
        if invalid_ids:
            raise serializers.ValidationError(
                "You can only share with families you belong to."
            )

        return value

    def validate(self, attrs):
        """Validate that at least one target is provided and expand meta families."""
        family_ids = attrs.get("family_ids") or []
        meta_family_ids = attrs.get("meta_family_ids") or []

        if not family_ids and not meta_family_ids:
            raise serializers.ValidationError(
                "Either family_ids or meta_family_ids must be provided."
            )

        if meta_family_ids:
            recipe = self.context.get("recipe")
            if recipe is None:
                raise serializers.ValidationError(
                    "Recipe context is required to share."
                )

            meta_ids = set(meta_family_ids)
            valid_meta_ids = set(
                FamilyGroupType.objects.filter(
                    family_id__in=meta_ids, type="META"
                ).values_list("family_id", flat=True)
            )
            invalid_meta_ids = meta_ids - valid_meta_ids
            if invalid_meta_ids:
                raise serializers.ValidationError(
                    "Meta families must be valid family networks."
                )

            connected_meta_ids = set(
                MetaFamilyMembership.objects.filter(
                    family=recipe.family, meta_family_id__in=meta_ids
                ).values_list("meta_family_id", flat=True)
            )
            not_connected = meta_ids - connected_meta_ids
            if not_connected:
                raise serializers.ValidationError(
                    "You can only share to meta families your family belongs to."
                )

            member_family_ids = list(
                MetaFamilyMembership.objects.filter(meta_family_id__in=meta_ids)
                .exclude(family__group_type__type="META")
                .values_list("family_id", flat=True)
                .distinct()
            )
            if not member_family_ids:
                raise serializers.ValidationError(
                    "Meta family has no member families to share with."
                )

            attrs["resolved_meta_family_ids"] = member_family_ids

        return attrs

class RecipeDraftUploadSerializer(serializers.Serializer):
    """Serializer for recipe screenshot upload."""

    screenshot = serializers.FileField(required=True)

    # Whitelist of permitted image content types and matching extensions.
    # Mirrors EventMediaViewSet/MediaStorageService.upload_file (image-only
    # subset; recipe drafts are screenshots, never videos).
    ALLOWED_CONTENT_TYPES = (
        "image/jpeg",
        "image/png",
        "image/gif",
        "image/webp",
        "image/heic",
        "image/heif",
    )
    ALLOWED_EXTENSIONS = (
        ".jpg",
        ".jpeg",
        ".png",
        ".gif",
        ".webp",
        ".heic",
        ".heif",
    )

    # First-bytes signatures for strict server-side type detection. Each
    # signature is ``(content_type, prefix_bytes, offset)``.
    _MAGIC_SIGNATURES: tuple[tuple[str, bytes, int], ...] = (
        ("image/jpeg", b"\xff\xd8\xff", 0),
        ("image/png", b"\x89PNG\r\n\x1a\n", 0),
        ("image/gif", b"GIF87a", 0),
        ("image/gif", b"GIF89a", 0),
        ("image/webp", b"RIFF", 0),  # RIFF...WEBP — full check below
        # HEIC/HEIF carries an ``ftyp`` box at offset 4 with a brand
        # like ``heic``, ``heix``, ``mif1`` etc.
        ("image/heic", b"ftypheic", 4),
        ("image/heic", b"ftypheix", 4),
        ("image/heif", b"ftypmif1", 4),
        ("image/heif", b"ftypmsf1", 4),
        ("image/heif", b"ftypheim", 4),
        ("image/heif", b"ftypheis", 4),
    )

    def validate_screenshot(self, value):
        """Validate the uploaded file is a real image.

        Defends against MIME smuggling by:
        - Refusing extensions outside the whitelist.
        - Refusing client-supplied content types outside the whitelist.
        - Sniffing the first bytes server-side and requiring a recognized
          image signature (so an attacker cannot rename ``evil.html`` to
          ``evil.jpg`` with ``Content-Type: image/jpeg``).
        """
        import os

        if value.content_type not in self.ALLOWED_CONTENT_TYPES:
            raise serializers.ValidationError(
                "Invalid file type. Allowed types: "
                f"{', '.join(self.ALLOWED_CONTENT_TYPES)}"
            )

        ext = os.path.splitext(value.name or "")[1].lower()
        if ext not in self.ALLOWED_EXTENSIONS:
            raise serializers.ValidationError(
                f"Invalid file extension '{ext}'. Allowed: "
                f"{', '.join(self.ALLOWED_EXTENSIONS)}"
            )

        # Max 10MB
        if value.size > 10 * 1024 * 1024:
            raise serializers.ValidationError("File size must be less than 10MB")

        # Byte-level magic check. Read up to 32 bytes from the front of
        # the file and reset the cursor for downstream consumers.
        head = value.read(32)
        try:
            value.seek(0)
        except Exception as exc:  # noqa: BLE001
            # Some uploaded-file backends are not seekable; FileField
            # tolerates re-reads from in-memory buffers. Log at debug
            # level so we have a breadcrumb without spamming production.
            logger.debug("Could not seek uploaded screenshot: %s", exc)

        if not self._matches_image_signature(head):
            raise serializers.ValidationError(
                "Uploaded file does not appear to be a valid image."
            )

        return value

    @classmethod
    def _matches_image_signature(cls, head: bytes) -> bool:
        if not head:
            return False
        for _, prefix, offset in cls._MAGIC_SIGNATURES:
            if (
                len(head) >= offset + len(prefix)
                and head[offset : offset + len(prefix)] == prefix
            ):
                # Special case: WebP requires both RIFF and WEBP markers.
                if prefix == b"RIFF":
                    if len(head) >= 12 and head[8:12] == b"WEBP":
                        return True
                    continue
                return True
        return False

Done. Summary:

**Fixed (high value):**
- `requirements.txt` — dropped unused `python-frontmatter`
- `recipes/models.py` — exposed `COOKLANG_PARSE_STATUS_NONE/VALID/INVALID` constants
- `recipes/cooklang.py` — derive `CLANCAL_UNITS` from `RecipeIngredient.UNIT_CHOICES`, `VALID_DIFFICULTIES` from `Recipe.DIFFICULTY_CHOICES` (no drift)
- `recipes/grocery_mapping.py` — derive `WEIGHT_UNITS` from `GroceryItem.WEIGHT_UNIT_CHOICES`, added return type
- `recipes/serializers.py` — replaced leaky `attrs["_parsed_cooklang"]` smuggle with `self._parsed_cooklang`; `_create_cooklang_children` now `bulk_create`s instead of N inserts; status strings → `Recipe.COOKLANG_PARSE_STATUS_*`; restructured Update validate so blank-title check fires for `cooklang_source=""` path; dropped "what" comments
- `recipes/api.py` — added 64KB size cap on `cooklang_preview` to bound parser CPU
- `recipes/management/commands/backfill_recipe_cooklang.py` — `iterator(chunk_size=500)` so prefetch actually applies (was N+1 in Django 5/6); use status constant
- `meals/services.py` — dropped "what" comments

**Skipped (intentional):**
- SimpleNamespace shim in `meals/services.py` — kwargs-API alternative was more verbose at 3 sites; advisor flagged "justified but awkward"
- Mixin extraction across Create/Update serializers — larger refactor, current helpers already deduplicate
- Dropping persisted `cooklang_parse_status`/`cooklang_parse_error` — schema decision, defer
- bulk_create in `_to_grocery_*` paths — merge-strategy per-item lookup makes it non-trivial
- Reverted error-message change in `cooklang.py` — `test_parse_rejects_source_without_body` pins original wording

**Not verified:** Docker daemon down on host, couldn't run `pytest`. All files pass `py_compile`. Recommend `make lint-fix && pytest recipes/ meals/` when daemon up.

76	        """Get recipes visible to the current user."""
77	        user = self.request.user
78	        if not user.is_authenticated:

from recipes.cooklang import parse_cooklang_source, render_cooklang_source
from recipes.models import Recipe, RecipeIngredient, RecipeStep
from users.models import FamilyGroup, FamilyMembership


def _user_with_family(username: str = "cooklang-user"):
    user = get_user_model().objects.create_user(
        username=username,
        email=f"{username}@example.com",
        password="testpass123",  # pragma: allowlist secret
    )
    family = FamilyGroup.objects.create(name=f"{username} Family")
    FamilyMembership.objects.create(
        user=user,
        family=family,
        role="PARENT",
        is_admin=True,
    )
    return user, family


def test_parse_cooklang_extracts_metadata_ingredients_steps_and_timers():
    source = """---
title: Beach Pancakes
description: Easy trip breakfast
servings: 4
time.prep: 10 minutes
time.cook: 15 minutes
difficulty: easy
source.url: https://example.com/pancakes
---

Mix @plain flour{125%g}, @milk{250%ml}, and @eggs{2}.

Cook on a #griddle{} for ~side{3%minutes}.
"""

    parsed = parse_cooklang_source(source)

    assert parsed.title == "Beach Pancakes"
    assert parsed.description == "Easy trip breakfast"
    assert parsed.servings == 4
    assert parsed.prep_time_minutes == 10
    assert parsed.cook_time_minutes == 15
    assert parsed.difficulty == "EASY"
    assert parsed.source_url == "https://example.com/pancakes"
    assert parsed.ingredients[0].name == "plain flour"
    assert parsed.ingredients[0].amount == Decimal("125")
    assert parsed.ingredients[0].unit == "g"
    assert parsed.ingredients[1].amount == Decimal("250")
    assert parsed.ingredients[1].unit == "ml"
    assert parsed.ingredients[2].amount == Decimal("2")
    assert parsed.ingredients[2].unit == "count"
    assert parsed.steps[0].instruction == "Mix plain flour, milk, and eggs."
    assert parsed.steps[1].timer_minutes == 3


def test_parse_rejects_source_without_body():
    with pytest.raises(ValueError, match="Cooklang recipe body is required"):
        parse_cooklang_source("---\ntitle: Empty\n---\n")


def test_render_cooklang_source_escapes_multiline_steps():
    rendered = render_cooklang_source(
        title="Toast",
        description="Simple",
        servings=1,
        prep_time_minutes=2,
        cook_time_minutes=3,
        difficulty="EASY",
        source_url="",
        ingredients=[
            {"name": "bread", "amount": Decimal("2"), "unit": "count", "notes": ""},
            {
                "name": "butter",
                "amount": Decimal("1.5"),
                "unit": "tbsp",
                "notes": "softened",
            },
        ],
        steps=[
            {"instruction": "Toast the bread.\nSpread butter.", "timer_minutes": None},
        ],
    )

    assert "title: Toast" in rendered
    assert "@bread{2}" in rendered
    assert "@butter{1.5%tbsp}(softened)" in rendered
    assert "Toast the bread.\\\nSpread butter." in rendered

# Skip if no upcoming events
                if not upcoming_events.exists():
                    logger.info(
                        f"No upcoming events for user {user.username}, skipping digest"
                    )
                    continue

                # Prepare event data with family names
                events_with_family = []
                for event in upcoming_events:
                    family_name = "Personal"
                    if event.family_group:
                        family_name = event.family_group.name

                    events_with_family.append(
                        {
                            "id": event.id,
                            "title": event.title,
                            "description": event.description,
                            "location": event.location,
                            "start_time": event.start_time,
                            "end_time": event.end_time,
                            "family_name": family_name,
                        }
                    )

                # Prepare email content
                subject = "Your Weekly Events Digest"
                from_email = settings.DEFAULT_FROM_EMAIL
                to_email = user.email

                # Skip if user has no email
                if not user.email:
                    logger.warning(
                        f"User {user.id} has no email address, skipping digest"
                    )
                    continue

                # Create plain text content
                text_content = f"Hello {user.first_name or user.username},\n\n"
                text_content += "Here's a summary of upcoming events for the next week from your families:\n\n"

                for event_dict in events_with_family:
                    text_content += f"- {event_dict['title']}\n"
                    text_content += f"  {event_dict['start_time'].strftime('%A, %B %d, %Y at %I:%M %p')} - {event_dict['end_time'].strftime('%I:%M %p')}\n"

                        text_content += f"  Location: {event_dict['location']}\n"
                    text_content += f"  Family: {event_dict['family_name']}\n\n"

    return local_now + timedelta(days=day_offset)

    preference = NotificationPreference.objects.filter(
        user=user,
        notification_type="ONBOARDING_TIPS",
        channel=NotificationDelivery.Channel.EMAIL,
    ).first()
    if preference is None:
        return True
    return preference.enabled


def _should_skip_onboarding_email(queue_entry: OnboardingEmailQueue) -> bool:
    from events.models import Event
    from trips.models import GroceryList, PackingList, Trip, TripMember, TripProperty
    from users.models import FamilyMembership

    user = queue_entry.user
    email_number = queue_entry.email_number

    if queue_entry.onboarding_track == UserProfile.ONBOARDING_TRACK_CALENDAR_FIRST:
        if email_number == 1:
            return user.profile.calendar_connected_at is not None
        if email_number == 2:
            return FamilyMembership.objects.filter(user=user).count() > 1
        if email_number == 3:
            return Event.objects.filter(creator=user).exists()
        return False

    created_trips = Trip.objects.filter(creator=user)
    if email_number == 1:
        return created_trips.exists()
    if email_number == 2:
        return (
            TripProperty.objects.filter(trip__creator=user)
            .filter(Q(property_url__gt="") | Q(description__gt=""))
            .exists()
        )
    if email_number == 3:
        return (
            TripMember.objects.filter(trip__creator=user).exclude(user=user).exists()
            or PackingList.objects.filter(trip__creator=user).exists()
            or GroceryList.objects.filter(trip__creator=user).exists()
        )
    return False


def _build_onboarding_email_context(
    queue_entry: OnboardingEmailQueue,
) -> dict[str, str]:
    copy = ONBOARDING_EMAIL_COPY[queue_entry.onboarding_track][queue_entry.email_number]
    user = queue_entry.user
    headline = copy["headline"]
    cta_label = copy["cta_label"]
    if (
        queue_entry.onboarding_track == UserProfile.ONBOARDING_TRACK_VACATION_FIRST
        and queue_entry.email_number == 1
        and user.profile.discovery_source == "regional_calendar"
    ):
        headline = "Your saved travel ideas are ready to become a real trip."
    elif (
        queue_entry.onboarding_track == UserProfile.ONBOARDING_TRACK_VACATION_FIRST
        and queue_entry.email_number == 3
    ):
        from trips.models import TripMember

        if TripMember.objects.filter(trip__creator=user).exclude(user=user).exists():
            cta_label = "Start a packing list"
    elif (
        queue_entry.onboarding_track == UserProfile.ONBOARDING_TRACK_VACATION_FIRST
        and queue_entry.email_number == 4
    ):
        from events.models import Event

        if Event.objects.filter(internal_calendar__trip__creator=user).exists():
            cta_label = "Connect your calendar"

    return {
        "subject": copy["subject"],
        "headline": headline,
        "body": copy["body"],
        "cta_label": cta_label,
        "cta_url": _onboarding_cta_url(queue_entry),
        "user_name": user.first_name or user.username,
    }


def sync_pending_onboarding_track_for_user(user, onboarding_track: str) -> int:
    """
    Update a user's onboarding track while the first onboarding email is still unsent.
    """
    if OnboardingEmailQueue.objects.filter(
        user=user,
        email_number=1,
        status=OnboardingEmailQueue.Status.SENT,
    ).exists():
        return 0

    updated = 0
    profile = user.profile
    if profile.onboarding_track != onboarding_track:
        profile.onboarding_track = onboarding_track
        profile.save(update_fields=["onboarding_track"])
        updated += 1

    updated += (
        OnboardingEmailQueue.objects.filter(
            user=user, status=OnboardingEmailQueue.Status.PENDING
        )
        .exclude(onboarding_track=onboarding_track)
        .update(onboarding_track=onboarding_track, updated_at=timezone.now())
    )
    return updated


def promote_onboarding_track_for_trip_creator(user) -> int:
    return sync_pending_onboarding_track_for_user(
        user, UserProfile.ONBOARDING_TRACK_VACATION_FIRST
    )


def enqueue_onboarding_emails_for_user(user, now=None) -> int:
    """Create or update the four onboarding emails for a verified user."""
    if not user.email or not is_user_email_verified(user):
        return 0

    profile = user.profile
    derived_track = profile.onboarding_track or derive_onboarding_track(profile)
    now = now or timezone.now()
    created_count = 0

    with transaction.atomic():
        sync_pending_onboarding_track_for_user(user, derived_track)

        for email_number, day_offset in ONBOARDING_EMAIL_DAY_OFFSETS.items():
            queue_entry, created = OnboardingEmailQueue.objects.get_or_create(
                user=user,
                email_number=email_number,
                defaults={
                    "onboarding_track": derived_track,
                    "scheduled_for": _schedule_onboarding_email_for_user(
                        user, now=now, day_offset=day_offset
                    ),
                },
            )
            if created:
                created_count += 1

    return created_count


@shared_task
def send_due_onboarding_emails(now=None) -> int:
    """Send onboarding emails that are due."""
    if now is None:
        now = timezone.now()

    due_entries = list(
        OnboardingEmailQueue.objects.select_related("user__profile")
        .filter(status=OnboardingEmailQueue.Status.PENDING, scheduled_for__lte=now)
        .order_by("scheduled_for", "email_number")
    )
    sent_count = 0

    for queue_entry in due_entries:
        user = queue_entry.user

        if not user.email or not is_user_email_verified(user):
            continue

        if not _onboarding_email_pref_enabled(user):
            queue_entry.status = OnboardingEmailQueue.Status.CANCELLED
            queue_entry.save(update_fields=["status", "updated_at"])
            continue

        if _should_skip_onboarding_email(queue_entry):
            queue_entry.status = OnboardingEmailQueue.Status.SKIPPED
            queue_entry.save(update_fields=["status", "updated_at"])
            continue

        try:
            context = _build_onboarding_email_context(queue_entry)
            html_content = render_to_string(
                "notifications/emails/onboarding_email.html", context
            )
            text_content = render_to_string(
                "notifications/emails/onboarding_email.txt", context
            )
            success = send_email(
                to_email=user.email,
                subject=context["subject"],
                html_content=html_content,
                text_content=text_content,
            )
            if success:
                queue_entry.status = OnboardingEmailQueue.Status.SENT
                queue_entry.sent_at = now
                queue_entry.last_error = ""
                queue_entry.save(
                    update_fields=["status", "sent_at", "last_error", "updated_at"]
                )
                sent_count += 1
            else:
                queue_entry.status = OnboardingEmailQueue.Status.FAILED
                queue_entry.last_error = "Email delivery returned failure"
                queue_entry.save(update_fields=["status", "last_error", "updated_at"])
        except Exception as e:
            logger.exception(
                "Failed to send onboarding email %s for user %s",
                queue_entry.email_number,
                queue_entry.user_id,
            )
            queue_entry.status = OnboardingEmailQueue.Status.FAILED
            queue_entry.last_error = f"Exception during email send: {e}"
            queue_entry.save(update_fields=["status", "last_error", "updated_at"])

    return sent_count


@shared_task
def process_notification_delivery(delivery_id):
    """
    Process a notification delivery

    Args:
        delivery_id: ID of the NotificationDelivery to process
    """
    try:
        delivery = NotificationDelivery.objects.select_related(
            "notification__user"
        ).get(id=delivery_id)

        # Skip if already processed
        if delivery.status not in ["PENDING", "FAILED"]:
            logger.info(
                f"Delivery {delivery_id} already processed with status {delivery.status}"
            )
            return

        # Update status to processing
        delivery.status = NotificationDelivery.Status.SENT
        delivery.save(update_fields=["status", "updated_at"])

        # Process based on channel
        channel = delivery.channel
        if channel == NotificationDelivery.Channel.EMAIL:
            _send_email_notification(delivery)
        elif channel == NotificationDelivery.Channel.IN_APP:
            # In-app notifications don't need additional processing
            delivery.status = NotificationDelivery.Status.DELIVERED
            delivery.delivered_at = timezone.now()
            delivery.save(update_fields=["status", "delivered_at", "updated_at"])
        elif channel == NotificationDelivery.Channel.PUSH:
            _send_push_notification(delivery)
        else:
            logger.warning("Unknown delivery channel: %s", channel)
            delivery.status = NotificationDelivery.Status.FAILED
            delivery.error_message = f"Unknown delivery channel: {channel}"
            delivery.save(update_fields=["status", "error_message", "updated_at"])

    except NotificationDelivery.DoesNotExist:
        # Non-actionable: caller scheduling now uses transaction.on_commit, but
        # log at warning so any rare residual race doesn't page Sentry.
        logger.warning("Delivery %s not found", delivery_id)
    except Exception as e:
        logger.exception("Error processing delivery %s: %s", delivery_id, e)
        try:
            delivery = NotificationDelivery.objects.get(id=delivery_id)
            delivery.status = NotificationDelivery.Status.FAILED
            delivery.error_message = str(e)
            delivery.retry_count += 1
            delivery.save(
                update_fields=["status", "error_message", "retry_count", "updated_at"]
            )

            # Retry if not too many attempts
            if delivery.retry_count < 3:
                process_notification_delivery.apply_async(
                    args=[delivery_id],
                    countdown=300,  # 5 minutes
                )
        except Exception as inner_e:
            logger.exception(f"Error updating delivery status: {str(inner_e)}")


@shared_task
def send_group_plan_followup_email_if_unread(notification_id: str) -> None:
    """Create email delivery for unread group plan notifications after a delay."""
    from notifications.models import Notification
    from notifications.services.notification_service import NotificationService

    try:
        notification = Notification.objects.select_related("user").get(
            id=notification_id
        )
    except Notification.DoesNotExist:
        logger.error("Group plan notification %s not found", notification_id)
        return

    if notification.notification_type != "GROUP_PLAN":
        logger.info(
            "Skipping non-group-plan follow-up for notification %s", notification_id
        )
        return

    if notification.read_at is not None:
        logger.info(
            "Skipping follow-up for read group plan notification %s", notification_id
        )
        return

    user = notification.user
    if not user.email:
        logger.info(
            "Skipping follow-up for group plan notification %s because user has no email",
            notification_id,
        )
        return

    from notifications.models import NotificationPreference

    email_pref_enabled = NotificationPreference.objects.filter(
        user=user,
        notification_type="GROUP_PLAN",
        channel=NotificationDelivery.Channel.EMAIL,
        enabled=True,
    ).exists()
    if not email_pref_enabled:
        logger.info(
            "Skipping follow-up for group plan notification %s due to disabled preference",
            notification_id,
        )
        return

    email_delivery_exists = (
        NotificationDelivery.objects.filter(
            notification=notification,
            channel=NotificationDelivery.Channel.EMAIL,
        )
        .exclude(status=NotificationDelivery.Status.FAILED)
        .exists()
    )
    if email_delivery_exists:
        logger.info(
            "Skipping follow-up for group plan notification %s because email is already queued or sent",
            notification_id,
        )
        return

    NotificationService._create_delivery(
        notification=notification,
        channel=NotificationDelivery.Channel.EMAIL,
    )
    logger.info(
        "Queued follow-up email delivery for unread group plan notification %s",
        notification_id,
    )


def _send_push_notification(delivery):
    """Send a push notification via Expo"""
    try:
        from notifications.services.expo_push_service import ExpoPushService

        notification = delivery.notification
        user = notification.user

        # Prepare notification data with deep link
        data = notification.data.copy() if notification.data else {}

        # Extract deep link if present
        deep_link = data.get("deep_link") or data.get("deepLink")
        if deep_link:
            # Expo will pass this to the app for handling
            data["url"] = deep_link
            data["deepLink"] = deep_link

        # Determine priority based on notification priority
        priority_map = {"HIGH": "high", "MEDIUM": "default", "LOW": "normal"}
        expo_priority = priority_map.get(notification.priority, "default")

        # Send to all user devices
        result = ExpoPushService.send_notification_to_user_devices(
            user=user,
            title=notification.title,
            message=notification.message,
            data=data,
            priority=expo_priority,
            client_app=data.get("client_app") or data.get("target_client_app"),
        )

        # Check if any notification was sent successfully
        if result.get("success", 0) > 0:
            with transaction.atomic():
                delivery.status = NotificationDelivery.Status.DELIVERED
                delivery.delivered_at = timezone.now()
                delivery.save(update_fields=["status", "delivered_at", "updated_at"])
            logger.info(
                f"Push notification delivered to {result['success']} devices for user {user.id}"
            )
        else:
            # All attempts failed
            error_msg = "No push notifications could be delivered"
            if result.get("failed", 0) > 0:
                error_msg += f" ({result['failed']} failed)"

            with transaction.atomic():
                delivery.status = NotificationDelivery.Status.FAILED
                delivery.error_message = error_msg
                delivery.save(update_fields=["status", "error_message", "updated_at"])

            logger.warning(f"Push notification failed for user {user.id}: {error_msg}")

    except Exception as e:
        logger.exception(f"Error sending push notification: {str(e)}")
        with transaction.atomic():
            delivery.status = NotificationDelivery.Status.FAILED
            delivery.error_message = str(e)
            delivery.save(update_fields=["status", "error_message", "updated_at"])
        raise


def _send_email_notification(delivery):
    """Send an email notification with transaction safety"""
    try:
        notification = delivery.notification
        user = notification.user

        # Skip if user has no email
        if not user.email:
            delivery.status = NotificationDelivery.Status.FAILED
            delivery.error_message = "User has no email address"
            delivery.save(update_fields=["status", "error_message", "updated_at"])
            return

        # Prepare email content
        subject = notification.title
        from_email = settings.DEFAULT_FROM_EMAIL
        to_email = user.email

        # Create plain text content
        text_content = f"{notification.message}\n\n"

        # Check if LLM enhancement is enabled for this user
        llm_enabled = feature_client.get_boolean_value(
            "enable-llm-in-email",
            False,
            EvaluationContext(
                targeting_key=str(user.id),
                attributes={
                    "email": user.email,
                    "groups": list(user.groups.values_list("name", flat=True)),
                },
            ),
        )

        if notification.data:
            # Add any additional data that might be relevant
            if (
                "event_title" in notification.data
                and "event_start_time" in notification.data
            ):
                text_content += f"Event: {notification.data['event_title']}\n"
                text_content += f"Time: {notification.data['event_start_time']}\n"

                # If LLM is enabled, enhance the message with additional context
                if llm_enabled:
                    logger.info(f"LLM enhancement enabled for user {user.id}")
                    # TODO: Add LLM enhancement logic here
                    # Example: Add personalized suggestions, weather info, etc.
                    pass

            elif "task_description" in notification.data:
                text_content += f"Task: {notification.data['task_description']}\n"

                # If LLM is enabled, enhance task notifications
                if llm_enabled:
                    logger.info(f"LLM enhancement enabled for user {user.id}")
                    # TODO: Add LLM enhancement logic here
                    # Example: Add task prioritization suggestions, time estimates, etc.
                    pass

        # Create HTML content
        context = {
            "notification": notification,
            "user": user,
            "llm_enhanced": llm_enabled,  # Pass to template
        }
        html_content = render_to_string(
            "notifications/email_notification.html", context
        )

        # Create and send email with transaction safety
        # Note: Email sending happens outside transaction since it's an external service
        # We update status after successful send to maintain consistency
        email = EmailMultiAlternatives(
            subject=subject,
            body=text_content,
            from_email=from_email,
            to=[to_email],
        )
        email.attach_alternative(html_content, "text/html")

        # Send email first (external operation)
        email.send()

        # Only update status if email was sent successfully
        # Using transaction to ensure atomic update
        with transaction.atomic():
            delivery.status = NotificationDelivery.Status.DELIVERED
            delivery.delivered_at = timezone.now()
            delivery.save(update_fields=["status", "delivered_at", "updated_at"])

        logger.info(f"Email notification sent to user {user.id}")

    except Exception as e:
        logger.exception(f"Error sending email notification: {str(e)}")
        # Update failure status with transaction safety
        with transaction.atomic():
            delivery.status = NotificationDelivery.Status.FAILED
            delivery.error_message = str(e)
            delivery.save(update_fields=["status", "error_message", "updated_at"])
        raise
